svg.title: Audio signal path through the ST-70 (one channel)
svg.desc: From RCA input through the 6GH8A pentode (gain), the 6GH8A triode (cathodyne phase splitter), the EL34 push-pull pair, the A-470 output transformer, to the speaker terminals. Feedback wire shown returning from the OPT to the pentode cathode.
svg.text: Audio signal path — one channel, end to end
RCA input → 6GH8A pentode (gain) → 6GH8A triode (phase split) → EL34 push-pull pair → A-470 → speaker

g.data-tooltip:
INPUT — RCA jack + input switch + 470 kΩ grid leak.
The RCA jack on the rear panel feeds the input switch (front), which selects between sources. A 470 kΩ grid leak resistor ties the pentode grid to ground, giving it a DC reference while presenting a high input impedance to the source.
Typical level here: ~1 Vpp line level.

6GH8A PENTODE — input voltage amplifier.
The signal arrives at the control grid; the pentode amplifies it by ~50× and outputs the larger AC swing at its plate. Plate sits at high DC (~150-200 V) so a coupling cap is needed to pass the signal to the next stage.
The pentode's CATHODE is where the global feedback returns (mixed with local cathode bias). Hover the dashed red wire below for the feedback summing.

COUPLING CAPACITOR — blocks DC, passes AC.
The pentode's plate sits at high DC voltage. The coupling cap passes the AC audio signal to the next grid while blocking that DC, so the triode's grid stays at its own designed bias point.
These caps age over decades; leaky coupling caps put DC on the next grid and skew bias. The #1 PC-3A failure mode.

6GH8A TRIODE — cathodyne phase splitter.
The triode has equal-value resistors above and below it (47 kΩ each, matched to 1%). Because the same current flows through both, the plate output and the cathode output have IDENTICAL amplitude but OPPOSITE phase — 180° apart. Exactly what push-pull needs.
This is the magic: one tube section + two equal resistors gives you a perfectly balanced phase-split signal, no calibration needed.
COUPLING CAP — blocks the triode plate's DC, passes AC to the EL34 grid.
COUPLING CAP — blocks the triode cathode's DC, passes AC to the other EL34 grid.

1 kΩ GRID STOPPER — suppresses RF parasitic oscillation.
Mounted directly at the EL34 socket (pin 5 to pin 6). Without it, the high-gain EL34 + the inductance of the lead wires can form an unintended RF oscillator at MHz frequencies.
1 kΩ GRID STOPPER — suppresses RF parasitic oscillation on the other EL34.

EL34 #1 (V2 left ch / V6 right ch) — receives the + phase signal at its grid (pin 5), bias holds it at ~50 mA idle, AC swings the plate current up and down. Its plate (pin 3) drives one end of the A-470 primary via the BLU/WHT lead.

EL34 #2 (V3 left ch / V7 right ch) — receives the − phase signal at its grid; plate current swings opposite to EL34 #1 at every instant. Its plate (pin 3) drives the other end of the A-470 primary via the BLUE lead. This is push-pull: the two tubes alternate driving the OPT primary's two halves.

B+ CENTER TAP — the RED lead on the A-470 primary brings B+ in at the middle of the winding. Push-pull plate currents balance around this point; the quiescent current draw on B+ is steady, only the AC swings oppositely in the two halves.

A-470 OUTPUT TRANSFORMER PRIMARY — center-tapped, push-pull.
The two halves of the primary (BLU/WHT lead and BLUE lead) are driven by EL34 plate currents that swing oppositely. Push-pull cancels DC magnetization in the core (so the core doesn't saturate on signal) and reinforces the AC signal in the secondary. Also rejects B+ ripple by common-mode cancellation.

A-470 SECONDARY — multiple impedance taps.
The secondary is a low-voltage, low-impedance winding with four taps: BLACK (common, 0 Ω reference), BROWN (4 Ω), ORANGE (8 Ω), YELLOW (16 Ω). Most modern speakers use ORANGE + BLACK. The YELLOW tap is also the global feedback sample point.

SPEAKER — the load.
Connected between the BLACK (common) and the appropriate impedance tap (typically ORANGE for 8 Ω speakers). Drives the air. The damping factor (how stiffly the amp resists speaker motion) is set by the OPT's secondary impedance plus any feedback-reduced output impedance.

FEEDBACK LOOP — from OPT secondary (16 Ω YELLOW tap) back to pentode cathode.
A single resistor (R_fb) samples the speaker-level signal and routes it back to the pentode's cathode. Because it sums there with opposite phase, the amp ends up controlled by the feedback ratio rather than open-loop gain. Trades ~16 dB of gain for ~16 dB lower distortion, output impedance, and bandwidth ripple.
A second wire from the UL primary tap provides HF stability compensation — see negative-feedback path page for both.
g.text: global negative feedback (from 16 Ω tap, through R_fb, to pentode cathode)

svg.text: Solid blue = positive-phase signal. Dashed blue = negative-phase signal (180° apart from the cathodyne).
Dashed red = negative feedback loop. Red = B+ feed at the OPT primary center tap.
Right channel is the mirror: substitute V6/V7 for V2/V3.
